title: The Three Griefs and the Four Weepings
description: T59 names the three compassions of the Lord over the soul in mingling: the Lord at the register of life-bearing grieves over the rational held fast within every form the proprium has taken; the Lord as Divine Human grieves whenever the rational cries out under the bonds and blows the proprium daily inflicts; the Lord at the register of the call going out also grieves (the third register breaks off in the surviving text). At every register the Lord bends in sorrow; his compassion is part of what works the soul's regeneration. T60 names the four weepings of the rational: three at descent, when the rational sees the proprium it must enter and yet goes in under necessity, then falls silent; and a fourth at the consummation, weeping over souls cut off from rest because they bound themselves wholly to self-love — even the firmaments share in this grieving.
